properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-04, while BL-186 was mid-build: "maybe we setup an exploratory brainstorm and branch discussing the various ways that we could mass-ingest something like in dev_storyflow. then we can systematically test some different strategies and observe/measure which performs the best." Nothing here is chosen, and no option below has been costed by running it.

THE CASE, MEASURED (dev_storyflow, `/home/ajs7/project/dev_storyflow`, read-only): 1,124 markdown files, 22 MB, ~6M tokens of source text. 17 files at depth 1 and 1,107 below it, so a non-recursive ingest reads 1.5% of the corpus and reports nothing missing. docs/archive 333 files / 16.2 MB (73% of the volume, dated superseded board snapshots); memory/ 380; docs/evidence 195 md + 744 binaries; the plausibly design-bearing remainder is 216 files / 3.3 MB. The fleet's own survey (`reflow2_feedback.md`, api-boss 07426210) read samples rather than filenames and found docs/evidence is at least FIVE types, and that 102 of 334 memory files are unbuilt product intent that reflow2 already models — so a filename-level exclusion of memory/ would be wrong.

(a) INGEST EVERYTHING, RECURSIVELY, NO SELECTION. Cheapest to specify, and the only option needing no human judgement. Expensive to run (~6M tokens before the per-pass multiplier) and the yield is poor: a design dominated by 333 superseded archives. Counter-argument that is specific rather than general — the archives are dated snapshots of the SAME few boards, so they are near-identical to each other, and the DUPLICATES bridge built for corpus-scale asking would turn them into thousands of standing questions. The mechanism that makes batched asking possible is the same one that makes an unselected corpus unusable.

(b) PLAN THEN INGEST (directory triage). Walk the tree, group by directory, report counts + bytes + sample names, put THAT to the user as one batched ask about scope before any document is extracted. Cheap, one round, and it puts the judgement where it belongs — reflow2 cannot know that `archive/` is superseded, and hardcoding a skip-list is the "shaping the model until the tool goes quiet" failure docs/sharpening.md names. Honest counter-argument: directory-level judgement is wrong at file level, and the fleet's own deeper read proves it — docs/evidence holds 5 runbooks and 50 root-cause memos that are knowledge, not evidence, and excluding the directory loses them.

(c) CLASSIFY THEN ROUTE. A cheap per-document classification pass first (design intent / evidence / archive / doctrine / hazard), then route by kind: intent gets the full extraction, evidence becomes an Artifact with an anchor, archive is skipped or marked pending_expansion. More calls but each tiny, and it matches what the corpus actually is rather than what its folders are named. Counter-argument: it adds a classifier whose errors are invisible, and it is the option most likely to quietly mis-file the thing you care about.

(d) EXPLOIT THE CORPUS'S OWN SELF-LABELLING. It already declares itself: 102/334 memory files say FUTURE/parked, evidence files pin commit SHAs, grounding docs are headed "READ-ONLY GROUNDING (no code, no build)". Zero model cost for the signal. Counter-argument, measured: 117 of 334 memory files declare no type at all, and the fleet's filename convention and its frontmatter schema already disagree (`tech_` is 67 by filename and 6 by declared type) — so the labels cover most of the corpus and are silent exactly where it is messiest.

(e) HIGH-VALUE-FIRST, INCREMENTALLY. Ingest docs/architecture (20), docs/decisions (6), docs/grounding (34), briefs and the root planning docs — the 216-file remainder — measure the design that results, then decide whether more is worth it. Fastest to first value, and it composes with the resume story already settled on BL-186 (the graph IS the resume point; sweep the folder, diff against registered Fragments, the remainder is the work left). Counter-argument: it answers "is this useful" and not "does this scale", which is the question BL-186 exists to answer.

WHAT A TRIAL WOULD HAVE TO MEASURE, since none of the above is decidable by argument: documents ingested per unit cost; nodes created against merge candidates raised (signal to noise); how many candidates a HUMAN then has to rule on; coverage_report claimed against unclaimed; and the only test that actually matters, which the scope doc already states — "whether an agent reading 500 heterogeneous markdown files produces a design a human recognises is a trial, not an argument, and it should be run on a real folder before anyone promises this to a user."
properties.name: OPEN — how should a corpus like dev_storyflow's 1,124 documents actually be mass-ingested?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the options survive as options. Anthony proposed trialling several strategies and measuring which performs best; this node holds the strategies, and dec:idea-trial-driven-choice-skill holds the separate question of whether reflow2 should have a way to run that kind of trial at all. Measurements of dev_storyflow are exact greps taken 2026-08-04; the type judgements are the fleet's own from reflow2_feedback.md, not mine — my earlier filename-level read of memory/ was wrong and is corrected above.
